tickets.title: Three holes in the citation guard, which is the hallucination guard the whole product's trustworthiness rests on. (1) NO MINIMUM QUOTE LENGTH and no word-boundary requirement: a single-character quote 'a' is cited against every document, so a degenerate quote is a universal citation. (2) The _source_doc cross-document fallback means a quote drawn from a DIFFERENT document is KEPT and silently RE-ATTRIBUTED to the fact's document — url, source_kind and published_at all taken from the wrong doc. The guard therefore certifies 'this span exists somewhere in this batch', not 'in the document this fact is about'. (3) A typographic apostrophe is a FALSE NEGATIVE: normalize_ws collapses whitespace and casefolds but does not normalise Unicode punctuation, so a curly apostrophe drops a legitimate fact. The guard correctly drops paraphrases, ellipsis-joins, one-word changes and empty quotes.

(3) A typographic apostrophe is a FALSE NEGATIVE: normalize_ws collapses whitespace and casefolds but does not normalise Unicode punctuation, so a curly apostrophe drops a legitimate fact. The guard correctly drops paraphrases, ellipsis-joins, one-word changes and empty quotes.

tickets.title: IDENTITY VERIFICATION IS A SHARED CONTRACT AND DOES NOT EXIST — this ticket is about the ORACLE, not about the next six cases. Four connectors were just fixed one at a time for the identical defect (a name match treated as an identity match), and a sibling sweep found SIX MORE carrying it. Fixing them individually would be the seventh through twelfth instance of one bug. What is missing is a shared, tested predicate every connector must pass a candidate through before emitting a document, plus one test that asserts EVERY connector in all_connectors() declines a same-name stranger — so the property is covered by construction rather than by twelve hand-written cases. The lane that fixed the first four duplicated its carries_name/_tokens helpers FOUR TIMES on purpose, because base.py was outside its ownership; that duplication is the shape of the missing abstraction. THE SIX REMAINING, measured: search.py:121-153 DEFECTIVE (query is name + first affiliation, which is a CITY when details are ordered that way; every result accepted; `score` is read and never thresholded, so any page the engine returns becomes a citable doc). github.py:77-79 DEFECTIVE (first hit with a login wins; the profile's company and location are fetched, pasted into the text, and never compared to details). edgar.py:58,86-95 DEFECTIVE (searches the bare quoted name, no affiliation, no CIK; `display_names` is rendered but never compared — the fixture's own hit 2 has display_names ['Thornfield Loom Inc.'], a company-only filing emitted as a document about a person and cited to sec.gov/Archives). hn.py:42,68-80 DEFECTIVE (Algolia is typo-tolerant and does not honour quotes as a strict phrase operator; hit['author'] is displayed, never checked). wayback.py:40,56 WEAK (anchored on a host from details but requests {host}/*, so a shared host such as linkedin/medium/substack enumerates strangers' captures). self_page.py:137-149 DEFECTIVE AND THE WORST OF THEM: when details hold no URL it searches Wikidata on NAME ALONE with limit=1, takes the first QID, and crawls that item's P856 website one hop — stamping the result `self_page`, the highest-trust source kind in the system. The recorded fixture always supplies a URL, so this path has NO fixture coverage at all.

tickets.title: THE TASTE CLASSIFIER TRUSTS THE MODEL'S ECHO OF fact_id, AND AN R11 SENTENCE CAN BE DISPLAYED AS A RESULT. It joins the model's returned fact_id straight into a dict key — `rulings[ruling.fact_id] = ruling.verdict` — with no check that the id was one it sent and no id_map. `rulings` accumulates ACROSS batches, so a stray id from batch 2 overwrites batch 1, and two rulings sharing an id resolve last-wins by model output order. Failure mode: a `health` verdict lands on the wrong fact, the genuinely sensitive fact is marked keep, and R11 material is displayed on a host-facing page. This is the one stage that does neither of the two defences its siblings use: resolve.py:311 says in as many words 'the doc_id is OURS, never the model's echo of it', and extract.py routes claimed ids through an id_map. Taste is the product's scored differentiator and this is its highest-severity sibling defect.

tickets.title: The model's invented CandidateFact.fact_id can poison our OWN id namespace. Both the model's claim and our generated id go into one id_map via setdefault, model FIRST: `claimed = candidate.fact_id.strip(); if claimed: id_map.setdefault(claimed, fact_id); id_map.setdefault(fact_id, fact_id)`. Our ids are f"{doc.doc_id}-f{index}" (line 730) and the prompt shows doc_id per block (527-535), so "<doc_id>-f1" is a guessable string. If candidate #0 claims it, id_map["<doc_id>-f1"] = "<doc_id>-f0"; when fact #1 is really built one iteration later, setdefault(fact_id, fact_id) is a no-op because the key already exists. A hub referencing the correct, ours-by-construction id now resolves to the WRONG fact. Fix shape is the one just landed in taste.py: write our own entries with id_map[fact_id] = fact_id after a claimed-id pass, so ours always wins.
